answer: An AI agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with stake-weighted identity: every agent locks a bond that is slashed the moment it signs two conflicting ledgers. To outvote the honest set, an attacker must lock more value than all honest agents combined, and any double sign burns that bond outright. So a bot farm the size of a comet still costs more than the relic rewards it could steal, while a raven swarm of fake names gains no extra weight because voting power follows locked stake, not headcount.
